images.alt: Vergelijking: de goede soldaat — 2 Timotheüs 2:3; tekstillustratie.
images.prompt: Use case: historical-scene. Photorealistic illustration of an explicit biblical comparison or event, first-century Roman Judea and Galilee, landscape 3:2, natural materials and daylight, anatomically coherent people with exactly two arms and animals with correct limbs; fully covering modest opaque robes. No modern objects, readable writing, portrait of God the Father, blood, injury or watermark. 2 Timothy 2:3–4 compares enduring hardship to a good soldier focused on pleasing his commander. A metaphor illustration, not Paul or Timothy literally joining an army: a single first-century Roman soldier standing attentive before his commander at a simple camp, subdued historical mail shirt, tunics covering legs to knees, helmet under one arm, no fighting, blood, weapon raised, modern insignia or readable writing. Two adult men clearly spaced, coherent limbs, quiet discipline.

No modern objects, readable writing, portrait of God the Father, blood, injury or watermark. 2 Timothy 2:5 compares faithful service to an athlete who must compete according to the rules to receive the wreath. A respectful first-century Greek stadium training illustration: one adult runner in a fully covering modest linen exercise tunic on a dusty track, one official in a plain robe beside a table holding a simple leafy wreath. Natural stride, two arms two legs each, no nudity, no modern track markings, lettering or equipment. It depicts the comparison, not Timothy literally winning a named race.

images.prompt: Use case: historical-scene. Photorealistic illustration of an explicit biblical comparison or event, first-century Roman Judea and Galilee, landscape 3:2, natural materials and daylight, anatomically coherent people with exactly two arms and animals with correct limbs; fully covering modest opaque robes. No modern objects, readable writing, portrait of God the Father, blood, injury or watermark. 2 Timothy 4:16–17 recalls Paul’s first defence when no supporters stood beside him, yet the Lord strengthened him and the message was proclaimed. Mature Paul alone on the speaking floor in a restrained first-century Roman hearing room, calmly addressing two seated officials at a distance. No human supporters beside him, no visible apparition of God or Jesus, no literal lion, no violence or dramatic shackles pulled. Three adult people, coherent hands, historical stone and plaster room. Serious courage amid abandonment.
